summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator, Checker, and Rio discuss how to disrupt Pithica's many revenue streams. The narrator's plan of mass warnings to victims is dismissed by Checker as lacking legitimacy, since the sources are spread across many banks and organizations worldwide. Checker proposes a Trojan that would alter the accounts, but the narrator argues people must move their money simultaneously, and the group needs an authority that only a shadowy multinational organization can provide. The narrator chooses to contact that group despite Checker's objections and asks Rio for a disposable phone.
one_line: The characters debate how to expose Pithica's revenue streams and decide to contact a dangerous shadowy organization for authority.
key_facts: The team expects to have a huge list of the exact paths of all Pithica's revenue streams, involving thousands of sources.
The narrator's original idea was to send massive tip-offs warning people they are being stolen from or that their money isn't going where they think.
Checker says the tip-offs would not be taken seriously because Pithica's network comes from all over the world.
The narrator notes the revenue sources span different banks, businesses and organizations, so a mass communication would be dismissed in less than zero time.
Checker proposes sending a Trojan that would alter the accounts so that people checking them see something happening.
The narrator argues nobody will check the accounts all at once, and everyone must move their money simultaneously so Pithica cannot respond.
The narrator says the group needs virtual psychic paper that grants authority to verify the message.
The narrator proposes contacting a shadowy multinational organization that can pull every string in the book.
Checker warns that the shadowy organization already said they would kill the narrator.
The narrator replies that the organization cannot do much worse than killing them.
Checker says the narrator will get their own way no matter how much he objects.
Rio opens a kitchen drawer containing disposable cell phones still in their packaging and hands one to the narrator.
Rio asks whether the plan is viable, and the narrator answers that it is what they have and that these are dangerous people.
Pithica knows the group is out there and has the information, so it is only a matter of time before Pithica tracks them down or changes its revenue structure.

entities.name: Pithica
entities.role: target organization whose revenue streams the group wants to expose; its network spans the world

entities.name: Checker
entities.role: companion who works at computers, objects to the plan, and proposes a Trojan

entities.name: Rio
entities.role: companion in the narrow kitchen who supplies a disposable cell phone

entities.name: shadowy multinational organization
entities.role: group that can provide the authority needed and has previously threatened to kill the narrator
